solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After fare's cut by pound, drunk's brightened up

indicators.note: the drunk piece comes after the cut fare, so it is written second
being cut by something means having it slice into the middle, so the pound letter goes inside the fare

parts.note: fare is food served at a meal
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner perks up once the bill for the meal is reduced by a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A floodlit pitch or building has been lit up brightly by powerful lamps, so brightened up fits.

clue.text: Iron-clad shell of uranium hit the roof

indicators.note: something clad is wrapped in an outer layer, so the iron symbol wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the shell is the outside, so take the first and last letters of uranium

explanation.surface: A uranium projectile in an iron casing, in the language of armaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron-clad' reads as one armour-plated adjective, but the hyphen hides two jobs: the metal, then the wrapping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to seethe with anger, the same idiom as going ballistic or hitting the roof.

clue.text: Stored in silo, a type of cereal

indicators.note: something stored in a silo is kept inside it, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A kind of grain kept in a farm silo.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaty describes something made of or tasting of oats, a cereal grain.

clue.text: Something easy, nursing doctor before a stroke

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the easy task holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a doddle is British slang for a very easy task

indicators.note: the doctor comes before the a, written first

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: An easy job for a nurse, looking after a doctor ahead of a stroke patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a medical scene with the doctor and nursing, but it is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog paddle is a simple swimming stroke, paddling with the arms below the surface like a dog.

clue.text: European football team calling for half-time?

parts.note: Inter Milan, known simply as Inter, is an Italian football club
a calling or vocation is one's mission in life

explanation.surface: A football club summoning its players back at half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is a break in the middle of a performance, which half-time is, for a match; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Rot from Conservative stars

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of stars and sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A political complaint that the Tory leadership is talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like nonsense spoken by Conservatives; it is decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is tooth decay, a rotting of the enamel and bone.

clue.text: Tax returns holding up a grant

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece holding up another sits beneath it, so the a comes first
returning means the tax word is read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax paid to use a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Tax rebates delaying payment of a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out a share, as one might grant funds or time.

clue.text: Lordly houses very unaffected

indicators.note: to house is to give shelter inside, so the lordly word contains the very letter

parts.note: imperious means haughty and domineering, like a lord

explanation.surface: Aristocrats' stately homes, quite untouched by the outside world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun after Lordly but is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impervious is not moved or harmed by something, so is unaffected by it.

clue.text: Replaced top cops and media bosses

parts.note: supers is short for superintendents, senior police officers
ED is short for editor, and two of them are needed for the plural

explanation.surface: Senior police and newspaper editors being ousted from their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superseded has been displaced by a newer thing taking its place.

clue.text: Commute time halved through big road opening

indicators.note: going through means being inside, so the halved time sits within the road and opening

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, read here as MI
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

indicators.note: halving keeps the first two of the four letters of time

explanation.surface: A commuter's journey time halved by a new motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commute' reads as daily travel, but it means reduce a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To commute a punishment is to lessen it, and to mitigate is to make it less severe.

clue.text: Overturned more than one schoolboy error

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, so the schoolboys are read in reverse order

parts.note: pupils are schoolchildren, plural here

explanation.surface: A spelling mistake made by a whole class, now corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a careless mistake, an informal word for error.

clue.text: People generally not forgiving insolence in former warzone

parts.note: we can stand for people in general, as in we all need sleep
stern means strict and unforgiving
front is cheek or brazen impudence

explanation.surface: A general observation that unforgiving people put up with rudeness in a former battleground.
explanation.definitionFit: The trench line in France and Belgium was the main battleground of the First World War, now long past.

clue.text: Maybe hear terror is what gives you a shock

indicators.note: maybe says the letters could be arranged another way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Hearing of terror is what frightens a person.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' is a mass of hair, not a fright: the lotion gives you a full head again.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick, bushy mass of hair, which a tonic for baldness aims to produce.

clue.text: In France, once, change a strongly acidic element in brass

parts.note: sous are old French coins of small value, small change formerly used in France
pH one, or PH ONE, marks a very strong acid on the pH scale

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson about a corrosive element found in the alloy brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' and 'element' suggest metal and chemistry; the brass is the brass section of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: This large coiled tuba is a member of the brass family, so it is one element of a brass band.

clue.text: Crouch down, about to pick up frame on US train

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the crouching word goes round the picking-up word

parts.note: to cower is to crouch down in fear
to catch is to pick up, as with a ball or an infection

explanation.surface: Someone stooping to collect a picture frame from an American railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The angled metal frame fitted on the front of American locomotives pushes livestock and debris off the track.

clue.text: Like an egg base for taco not binding

indicators.note: the base of a word is its final letter in an across answer, so the last letter of taco

parts.note: a void contract is invalid and not legally binding

explanation.surface: A recipe note that egg is used as a base for tacos but not as a binder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, from the Latin word for an egg.

clue.text: One figure touring river or part of canal?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so one and the figure surround the river

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number
the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing

explanation.surface: A boat trip along a river or a stretch of canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, the digestive tract, not a waterway; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowel forms a long section of the alimentary canal, the body's digestive tract.

clue.text: Legal man, then, with legal men

parts.note: so can mean then, as in so you agree
licit means permitted by law
OR, other ranks, refers to ordinary soldiers, the men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A lawyer in the company of other lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: This lawyer advises clients and prepares legal documents, a professional in law.

clue.text: Win over queen's follower

parts.note: a success is a win or triumph
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Defeating a monarch's heir in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes next, taking over a role or title, follows the previous holder.

clue.text: Bachelor's taken off woman's top, the cad!

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so the bachelor's letter comes out

parts.note: a blouse is a woman's shirt-like top
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A shocked reaction to a man removing a woman's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' reads as undressing; it is the removal of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible man, the same insult as a rotter or a heel.

clue.text: Government building's aide getting wine out to chill

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
tent is a deep red Spanish wine used in communion
off means away or out, as in the lights are off
to ice is to make something cold

explanation.surface: An official's assistant putting wine outside to cool.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The state agency granting rights to inventions is a government department with its own offices.

clue.text: It's almost time when I should retire

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

explanation.surface: Someone noticing that it is almost bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here means going to bed, which one normally does after dark.

clue.text: Foreign land mass? Clay's beneath it

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is beneath comes lower, so the boxer follows the mass letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
Cassius Clay was the birth name of the boxer Muhammad Ali

explanation.surface: A geology question about the soil of a distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: Clay looks like soil; it is the boxer, and the 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked West African republic is a country abroad, so a foreign land.

clue.text: Drink up to get a quid

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the drink word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to gulp is to drink quickly in large mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Finishing a drink to earn a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' looks like a pound coin; here it is a piece of chewing tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a cake of pressed tobacco, a chunk of which is chewed as a quid.

clue.text: Where bird may be seen running and tripping?

parts.note: on means working or running, as with an engine
tripping is slang for being high on drugs

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher wondering where to spot a bird that runs and stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are seen up above in the sky, the phrase meaning aloft.

clue.text: Pet circles round track in some fine attire

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so the pet surrounds the round letter

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
O is round in shape
to tail is to follow or track someone

explanation.surface: A cat running laps round a track in elegant clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The long back part of a formal tailcoat is a piece of fine evening dress.

clue.text: Bloomers live to the west around desert

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the reversed live word goes round the deserter
in an across answer, west is leftward, so the live word reads backwards

parts.note: are means exist or live, as in we are
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: Flowers growing west of a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests flowers or underwear; it means blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a blunder, and errata is a list of mistakes in a printed book.

clue.text: Impassioned bird call

parts.note: bird and stir are both slang for a prison sentence
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: An excited bird's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is slang for prison time, as is stir, not a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirring speech is rousing and full of emotion, so impassioned.
